sentences.text: The name Sclerorhynchus translates to 'hard snout', reflecting the robust nature of its jaw structure.
The genus Sclerorhynchus was first described by Woodward in 1889.
This animal belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes sharks, rays, and their extinct relatives.
It is classified within the family Sclerorhynchidae.
The type species of the genus is Sclerorhynchus atavus, serving as the reference point for the group.
Other known species include S. leptodon, S. pettersi, S. fanninensis, S. priscus, and S. karakensis.
The genus Ganopristis is now treated as a junior synonym of Sclerorhynchus.
The time range for Sclerorhynchus spans from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
Fossils of Sclerorhynchus have been found in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, and North America.
